chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), whenever he went out, would say: 'O Allah, by You I go out, and to You I submit, and in You I believe, and upon You I rely. O Allah, bless for me this day of mine, and grant me its success, its victory, its help, its purification, its guidance, and its blessing, and turn away from me its evil and the evil of whatever is in it. In the name of Allah, and by Allah, and Allah is the Greatest, and the praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, I have gone out, so bless me in my going out and benefit me with it.'
He said, 'And whenever he entered his house, he said that (as well).'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited when leaving the house according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication reflects the Imams' emphasis on sanctifying daily transitions through dhikr, linking physical movement with spiritual reliance (tawakkul). It serves as a practical framework for believers to seek divine protection and success, mirroring the Quranic concept of seeking refuge in God from all evil.
